links.targetTitle: A primitive marked Globally Active with no Instances is auth

title: A Primitive can be Globally Active while its key deployment parameters are still unspecified
content:
The Agent Token Primitive's Global Activation Status is `Active` (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.4.1.1) and its Single Instance carries hard parameters — token name, symbol AGENT7, Genesis Supply, and the irreversible emissions lock. Yet three of the same parameter set are open: the token address (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.4.2.1.1.4) and token Admin (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.4.2.1.1.5) "will be specified in a future iteration of the Launch Agent 7 Artifact," and the Operational Process Definition for "minting and initial distribution of the tokens from the Genesis Supply" says only "These processes will be defined in a future iteration" (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.4.2.1.2). The Agent's Genesis Account is likewise deferred (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.1.3.1.1.4).

So the Artifact is designed to be *partially* binding. Commitments that constrain future behaviour (fixed supply, no Agent-level mint authority) are locked in first; facts that depend on deployment (addresses, admins, distribution mechanics) land later.

That ordering is defensible — you can promise not to mint before you know what address you will mint at — but it has a consequence worth flagging: the parameters that determine *who controls* the token are exactly the deferred ones. Until the Admin is specified, the strength of the emissions guarantee cannot be independently verified on-chain, only read from the document.

It also means Global Activation Status signals intent and authorization, not deployment completeness. Reading `Active` as "live and fully specified" would be a mistake.
description: The Agent Token Primitive is Active, yet AGENT7's contract address, token Admin, and the minting and initial distribution processes are all deferred to a future Artifact iteration.
